title: FERAL-7B SEC Season 00 operational rights review
summary: The exact frozen releases are cleared for access-controlled project materialization, private training, and private evaluation in the United States. The decision relies primarily on the SEC's express public-EDGAR reuse policy and lawful public acquisition. It does not claim that private filer text is a United States Government work or public domain, and it does not permit raw corpus redistribution or a product that reconstructs filing text.

basis.authority: United States Securities and Exchange Commission
basis.title: Webmaster Frequently Asked Questions
basis.finding: The SEC says that EDGAR public filing content is free to access and reuse. This is the direct reuse policy for the corpus source material.

basis.authority: United States Securities and Exchange Commission
basis.title: Privacy Information and Website Dissemination
basis.finding: The SEC says information on sec.gov is public and may be copied or further distributed without SEC permission, requests citation, and forbids misuse of SEC seals, logos, artwork, and marks.

basis.title: 17 U.S.C. sections 105 and 107
basis.finding: Section 105 applies to United States Government works, not automatically to private filings. Section 107 requires a case-specific fair-use analysis.

basis.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 3: Generative AI Training
basis.finding: The report treats training as fact-specific. Research and analysis uses with lawful sources and controls against source reproduction are more favorable than uses that create substitutes or rely on pirated copies.

basis.authority: United States Copyright Office Fair Use Index
basis.title: Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc., 788 F. Supp. 3d 1026 (N.D. Cal. 2025)
basis.finding: A district court found the training use before it fair, while stressing output substitution and market harm. The decision is fact-specific and is not the primary basis for this review.

basis.authority: United States Copyright Office Fair Use Index
basis.title: Bartz v. Anthropic PBC, 787 F. Supp. 3d 1007 (N.D. Cal. 2025)
basis.finding: The index records a mixed result: model training was treated differently from maintaining a library built from unlawfully acquired copies. FERAL uses public SEC archive sources, not shadow libraries.

corpus_scan.method: Case-insensitive line scan of all 303,482 JSONL examples for confidential, reproduction, distribution, copyright, proprietary, and third-party language.
corpus_scan.interpretation: Counts overlap and are screening signals, not findings that every match is a valid restriction. They show that the corpus contains long private-party filing excerpts and embedded notices, so raw redistribution and verbatim model output need stronger controls than factual analysis.

allowed_uses: Copy the exact frozen releases into access-controlled United States project storage.
Use the exact frozen training release for private FERAL-7B training after a separate dispatch authorization.
Use the exact frozen evaluation releases for private scoring after a separate evaluation authorization.
Create and share internal aggregate metrics, hashes, lineage records, and short attributed excerpts needed for audit and citation checks.
prohibited_uses: Publish or redistribute the raw filings, JSONL files, release archives, or a substantially equivalent text collection.
Build or expose a service whose purpose or practical effect is to reconstruct long filing passages or replace access to the filings.
Use the SEC seal, logos, artwork, or marks in a way that suggests SEC sponsorship or affiliation.
Treat private filer text as public domain solely because it was filed with the SEC.
conditions: Keep accession numbers, SEC archive URLs, filing dates, issuer identifiers, and source hashes with every example.
Limit project inputs to the exact lawfully collected public EDGAR archive objects bound by the three frozen release manifests.
Keep raw corpus storage private, access-controlled, logged, and limited to people and services working on FERAL-7B.
Before any public model, weights, or API release, run targeted memorization and verbatim-output tests and complete a separate release rights review.
Block or truncate long source-like output and prefer factual answers with short attributed quotations and SEC links.
Maintain an exclusion and takedown path for a valid rights, privacy, correction, withdrawal, or non-public-filing complaint.
Reopen this review if the corpus changes, the source moves beyond public SEC EDGAR content, the deployment leaves the United States, or governing law or SEC policy materially changes.
